pushHint.unsupported: This browser does not support push notifications.
pushHint.install: On iPhone and iPad, notifications only work after adding Synchaven via Share → Add to Home Screen and opening it from there (iOS 16.4 or later).
pushHint.insecure: Notifications only work when Synchaven is accessed via HTTPS.
pushHint.denied: Notifications are blocked for this site in the browser. Please allow them in the site settings.
pushHint.off: Reminders for events and due tasks appear as notifications, even when Synchaven is not open.
pushHint.on: Reminders are sent to this browser. They are set per event or as a default per calendar; tasks remind when due (all-day ones at 09:00).

dav.copyFailed: Copying is not possible – please select the text
dav.title: Sync with DAVx⁵
dav.intro: Contacts can be synced via CardDAV with Android (DAVx⁵), Thunderbird or iPhone/iPad. Changes on the phone appear here and vice versa.
dav.insecure: The connection is not encrypted. For syncing over the internet, put a reverse proxy with HTTPS in front, since the password is sent with every request.
dav.howTo: How to set it up in DAVx⁵
dav.step1: Open DAVx⁵ and tap {plus} at the bottom right.
dav.step2Option: Login with URL and user name
dav.step3: Enter the base URL, user name and password from above and tap {login}.
dav.step4: Confirm the account name (preferably the email address) and tap {create}.
dav.step5: Enable the address books you want in the {tab} tab.
dav.otherClients: Thunderbird and iOS find the address books automatically with the same address (iOS: Settings → Contacts → Accounts → Other → CardDAV account).
dav.appPasswordRequired: With two-factor authentication on, CardDAV only accepts app passwords.
dav.appPasswordHint: Instead of your password you can use an app password, which you can revoke at any time.

backup.replaceText: All data of all users will be deleted and replaced by the content of “{file}” – including accounts and passwords. This cannot be undone. If your account is not in the export, you will be signed out.
backup.title: Export and import the database
backup.intro: Back up the whole database with all users, password hashes and settings (without push subscriptions) as JSON, e.g. before an update. The import replaces all existing data.
backup.exportConfirmText: The export contains all data of all users, their password hashes and the two-factor secrets. Confirm it with your password; the file is encrypted with a passphrase of your choice.
backup.passphraseHint: Needed for the import – without it the file cannot be restored
backup.importPassphraseText: This export is encrypted. Enter the passphrase that was chosen when exporting it.
backup.cliHint: The export also works while the server is running, e.g. for regular backups. With EXPORT_PASSPHRASE set in your environment (at least 12 characters) the file is encrypted:

logs.subtitle: The last {count} messages since the server start (level set via {variable})

overview.configHint: Set via environment variables; takes effect after a restart.
overview.vapidHint: Some push services require a real contact address in {variable}.

adminSettings.registrationHint: When registration is closed, you create new accounts under {users}. When running on the internet, it is best to close it after creating your own accounts.
adminSettings.tokenTtlHint: How long the web UI and the app stay signed in; the app extends the session when syncing. Applies to new sign-ins.

userDialog.savedSignedOut: Saved – the account was signed out on all devices
userDialog.nameHint: If empty, the part before the {'@'}
userDialog.passwordHintNew: Pass it on to the user; they can change it in their profile.
userDialog.passwordHintChange: Signs the account out on all devices and revokes its app passwords. CardDAV clients need the new password or a new app password afterwards.
userDialog.passwordHintOwn: Revokes your app passwords – CardDAV clients need a new one afterwards.
userDialog.ownRights: You cannot revoke your own rights
userDialog.adminHint: Administrators may open this administration: edit accounts, change settings and export and replace the whole database.
userDialog.languageHint: The account’s calendar, task list and address book are created in this language.
userDialog.resetTotpHint: E.g. if the phone with the authenticator app is lost. The account can then sign in with the password alone and set it up again.

users.disableText: {name} ({email}) is signed out immediately and can no longer sign in or sync until you enable the account again. The data is kept.
users.signOutText: {name} has to sign in again in the web UI and the app. CardDAV clients such as DAVx⁵ use the password or an app password and stay connected – for that, change the password (this also revokes all app passwords) or revoke a single app password in the account’s security settings.
users.deleteText: {name} ({email}) is deleted with all calendars, events, contacts and tasks ({stats}). This cannot be undone.
users.devices: notifications in {n} browser | notifications in {n} browsers

calendarView.deleteSeries: All events in this series will be deleted.
calendarView.moveOccurrenceText: Only the event on {date} is moved and detached from the series.
calendarView.deleteTaskWithSubtasks: “{name}” and one subtask will be deleted. | “{name}” and {n} subtasks will be deleted.
calendarView.deleteListText: “{name}” and all its tasks will be deleted permanently.
calendarView.deleteCalendarText: “{name}” and all its events will be deleted permanently.

contactsView.deleteContactText: “{name}” will be deleted – also on synced devices.
contactsView.deleteBookText: “{name}” and the contact in it will be deleted permanently. | “{name}” and all {n} contacts in it will be deleted permanently.
contactsView.deleteCategoryText: “{name}” will be removed from one contact. The contact itself is kept. | “{name}” will be removed from {n} contacts. The contacts themselves are kept.
contactsView.emptyHint: Create a contact, import a .vcf file (also via drag & drop) or sync with DAVx⁵.
contactsView.renameHint: Applies to all contacts. If the new name already exists, both categories are merged.

security.title: Security
security.twoFactorIntro: Signing in then also needs a code from an authenticator app on your phone (e.g. Aegis, Google Authenticator, 2FAS).
security.recoveryCodesLeft: No recovery codes left – please create new ones. | {n} recovery code left. | {n} recovery codes left.
security.scan: Scan the QR code with your authenticator app.
security.qrAlt: QR code for the authenticator app
security.manualEntry: Or enter this key in the app:
security.confirmHint: Enter the code the app shows to finish the setup.
security.recoveryCodesWarning: Keep these codes in a safe place. Each one signs you in once without the app – e.g. if your phone is lost. They are shown only now.
security.recoveryFileHeader: Synchaven recovery codes for {email} – each code works once
security.regenerateText: Your previous recovery codes stop working. Please confirm with your password and a code from the app.
security.disableText: Signing in then only needs your password again. Please confirm with your password and a code from the app.
security.appPasswordsIntro: For sync apps like DAVx⁵ or Thunderbird: they sign in with an app password instead of your password, and you can revoke it per device.
security.appPasswordsIntroTotp: For sync apps like DAVx⁵ or Thunderbird: with two-factor authentication on, CardDAV only accepts app passwords.
security.newAppPasswordIntro: Give it a name that tells you where it is used. Please confirm with your password.
security.appPasswordCreated: Enter this password as the password in “{name}”:
security.appPasswordOnce: The password is shown only now. If you lose it, simply create a new one.
security.revokeText: Apps that use “{name}” can no longer sync.
security.twoFactorIntroOn: Signing in needs a code from your authenticator app in addition to your password.
